title: Derived geometric stalk of a constant local model
statement: Let $f:U\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ a commutative ring. Use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], their constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and let $E^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules; write $\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ for its termwise constant sheaf complex [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. Suppose an isomorphism $\alpha:f^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{E^\bullet}_U$ is given, where $f^{-1}$ is the exact constant-coefficient module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. For every geometric point $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], put $\bar x=f\circ\bar u$. Applying the exact stalk functor termwise to representatives of $\alpha$ gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $K_{\bar x}\xrightarrow{\sim}E^\bullet$ in $D(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Here $K_{\bar x}$ is the derived object obtained by termwise geometric stalks; its coefficient ring is identified with $A$ by the constant-section stalk map. No boundedness, finiteness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09BI (lemma-connected-ctf-locally-constant), proof: the constant ring complexes on overlapping etale cover members are identified by a geometric stalk. Agent extraction of this derived-stalk comparison, using exact stalks and module-linear inverse-image composition.

proof.text: Let F be the ModuleCat A-valued sheaf fibre at ubar and G the fibre at ubar followed by f. The already proved generic source-library natural isomorphism Etale.upperStarCompSheafFiberIso (ModuleCat A) f ubar identifies upperStar f followed by F with G. This is lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar, applied directly in ModuleCat A. Both fibre functors are additive and exact by the Point.sheafFiber API. All maps are A-linear because the comparison is constructed in ModuleCat A; no separate passage through abelian groups or SheafOfModules is needed.

Use Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso on the comparison of Step 1, take its inverse at K, and compose with Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso (upperStar f) F at K. This identifies the derived stalk G_D(K) with F_D((upperStar f)_D(K)). Apply F_D to the given isomorphism alpha. Finally use F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors at the termwise constant complex to identify the result with Q of its termwise F-image. These are the exact-functor localization comparisons, valid for unbounded complexes.

The constant-stalk comparison is available in the proved generic source-library form Point.constantSheafCompSheafFiberIso, specialized to ModuleCat A. The forgetful functor on ModuleCat A preserves filtered colimits in universe u by preservesFilteredColimitsOfSize_shrink. Thus for c = constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat A), this gives a natural isomorphism c followed by F with the identity. Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso maps this natural isomorphism to a chain isomorphism from the termwise F-image of c(E) to the identity functor applied termwise to E. Compose with Functor.mapHomologicalComplexIdIso and apply Q.mapIso. Naturality gives compatibility with every differential, and all components are module homomorphisms.

Compose the isomorphism of Step 2 with the image under Q of the chain isomorphism of Step 3, and return it in Nonempty. Its source is definitionally geometricStalk A (ubar followed by f) applied to K. There are no boundedness, finiteness or Tor-amplitude conditions.

Step 3: the constant-stalk iso, with the scalar and differential equations written out, gives a chain iso. Step 4 is elementary composition. Every cited unit (sk-thm-properbasechange, sk-def-exchange, sk-thm-p1, sk-def-pbc) is in the transitive uses of sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so the 3 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic tools.
